name: OpenStax
goodFor: Free peer-reviewed textbooks for college and high school.

evidence.quote: OpenStax has transitioned our textbook library from a mix of CC BY and CC BY-NC-SA licensing to CC BY-NC-SA licensing across the library.
This change will apply to all newly released and updated versions of our titles, with limited exceptions.

Each individual work in the Service is offered for license to you by the author of that work on the terms and conditions set forth in the Creative Commons license associated with that individual work.
This book may not be used in the training of large language models or otherwise be ingested into large language models or generative AI offerings without OpenStax's prior written permission.

If you are redistributing all or part of this book in a noncommercial digital format, then for every page that includes OpenStax content, you must license the derivative work under the same CC-BY-NC-SA license as the original, and include on every digital page view the following attribution: Access for free at

The OpenStax name, OpenStax logo, OpenStax book covers, OpenStax CNX name, and OpenStax CNX logo, and Rice University name, and Rice University logo trademarks, or wordmarks are not subject to the Creative Commons license and may not be reproduced without the prior and express written consent of Rice University.
(Commercial entities should contact OpenStax to discuss reuse rights and permissions.)

notes: Checked book by book (see parts) against three of OpenStax's own records for each: its book record in the site's CMS, the book's preface in the site's content archive, and the licence block on its reader page. Every book is link only. On 22 April 2026 OpenStax moved its library to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for new and updated versions, which settles the earlier conflict: Concepts of Biology, once CC BY 4.0, now reads CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in all three places, like Biology 2e. Two live high-school books (Physics, Statistics) and the retired first editions still say CC BY 4.0 in their records and prefaces, but their reader pages describe noncommercial-only terms; that contradiction is for OpenStax to settle, so they stay link only too. Every reader page also says the book may not be used to train, or be ingested into, large language models or generative AI offerings without OpenStax's written permission, which matters for an AI tutor reading a student's OpenStax files and is one more reason the bank's agents don't read it. Where a book is reused at all, OpenStax asks for "Access for free at" and the page's address on every page view. The OpenStax and Rice University names, logos and book covers aren't covered by the licence. Nothing from OpenStax goes into the bank.
